why: “In your opponent’s Movement phase, if an enemy unit ends a move within 8" of this unit … this unit can make a Normal move of up to D6"”: movement, their turn, and nothing else. Same judgement as the other two lists that have the Goremongers datasheet (standard, super-terminators). The text is now Wahapedia's (bold Engagement Range and Normal move) in all three lists. Wahapedia, the GW faction pack and BSData all print a straight apostrophe in “opponent's”. The curly one is the house style the other lists' texts use, so it is not a source correction, but it doesn't change the timing.

It only removes items with a:'rule' whose v is one of the open list's army rules. In defenceItems those are the army rules' own def lines and Waaagh!'s ‘Riled up: 5+ INV’ (Orks have no RULE_OPTIONS). A unit ability is a:'ability', so an ability that happens to share an option's name can't be hidden. FNP lines from the Rules line have v:'Feel No Pain N+', which is never an army-rule name, and detachment rules are named ‘… · X rule · …’. I checked all 17 lists: the only line it hides is Martial Ka’tah's def ‘Kaptaris (start of the Fight phase…)’, on the five lite-knights unit screens. Those are exactly the snapshot changes, plus the curly-apostrophe Martial Ka’tah popup that only that chip opened. The Rules line still opens the rule. It's only used on screenUnit. One small thing, outside this function: RULE_OPTIONS also lists ‘Example’ as an option of Martial Ka’tah (it comes from the rule's ‘Example: If you selected the Solar Watch detachment…’ paragraph), so a Custodes army-rule def that started with ‘Example ’ would also be hidden. No def does that today.

I diffed main 24781aa's data.js against this branch's resolved lists for all 17 lists. Every field is the same apart from the five declared corrections and key order. The key-order changes are in 64 objects: weapon rows now have name before who/n, abilities have who before tag, and partialRules, kwOnly, mods and aura have moved within units. No datasheet in use has two rows of one name in a kind, and no RegExp values, so first-match lookup and the JSON copy are both safe. Hidden fields (ds, over, of, why, faction, bsId, gistOf, defOf) don't reach units or rows. A unit without ds is passed through unchanged, so in the old form its defOf/why aren't hidden. That's why `--expand` then `--write` is refused (see the report); it isn't a fault in the resolution itself.
